findings.title: Remove const from the mutating object parameter
findings.summary: On a successful positive-count result, func_00156dec writes halfwords directly into the supplied object at offsets 2*i and 0x40+2*i; the input is not merely used to locate separately mutable storage. Declaring both the wrapper and receiving function with const void * therefore advertises a read-only contract for a mutating operation and admits read-only objects that the implementation overwrites. Make the object parameter writable in both declarations.

evidence: Independently regenerated/read packets/func_00156dec.md: input saved in r4; final copy computes object+2*i and writes halfwords at +0/+0x40 on the positive-count path.
Canonical match result is MATCH with one branchnop: byte equality does not check the const contract against this original receiving body.

findings.subject: src/wave4/func_00166eac.c:3-7
findings.title: Forward both incoming floating-point coordinates
findings.summary: When the selected screen entry exists, func_00166eb0 immediately stores incoming s0 and s1 into that entry and its display object before defining either register. They are two floating-point inputs, but neither the wrapper nor its callee declaration exposes or forwards them. A C call through this two-argument interface cannot provide the intended coordinates and the receiver consumes unspecified values. Add the two float parameters to both signatures and forward them; the tail branch matching after branchnop does not establish argument completeness.

The canonical wrapper is MATCH with a single branchnop despite omitting the VFP arguments from its source interface.

findings.subject: src/wave4/func_001c3abc.c:3-7
findings.title: Declare the fourth argument as a UTF-16 text pointer
findings.summary: The fourth register is not an integer mode: when the selected text object is enabled, func_001c3ac0 treats it as a nullable text pointer, substitutes a default string for null, reads successive halfwords, copies them into an embedded text buffer, and passes that buffer to func_00170c20. The int mode declaration misrepresents this pointee contract, rejects ordinary text-pointer callers without a cast, and permits selector-like values to be dereferenced as addresses. Use a nullable const unsigned short *text parameter in the wrapper and receiving declaration.

Independently regenerated/read packets/func_00170c20.md: receiving text path scans the forwarded halfword buffer to its terminator and dispatches it as text.

findings.subject: src/wave4/func_001229d0.c:3-7
findings.title: Type the registered callback as a function pointer
findings.summary: For index values below seven, func_001229d4 stores the first argument into context+0x10+4*index. The event worker func_00137984 later loads that exact slot, null-checks it, and invokes it with BLX; existing initialization installs function addresses there. This is a callable callback, not a data buffer. The void *buffer interface accepts non-callable data and requires a nonportable object/function-pointer conversion for actual callbacks. Give the callback parameter a function-pointer type in both the wrapper and receiving declaration and forward that type consistently.

findings.subject: src/wave4/func_00121bc4.c:3-7
findings.title: Accept a writable object pointer instead of an unsigned mode
findings.summary: The receiving func_00121bc8 preserves the input as an object address and ultimately passes it to func_0012edd4, which adds an embedded-link offset and directly reads and rewrites the object links. The original caller func_0019dd28 corroborates this by passing the address of its embedded member at +0x18. This is a writable object-pointer contract, not an unsigned mode: the new declarations require a pointer-to-integer conversion to pass the real object and hide its mutability. Accept an appropriate node pointer or opaque void * in both wrapper and receiving declaration. The existing ARM tail branch preserves the bits; this is a source-interface defect, not demonstrated address truncation or a byte-match failure.

qualifications: Scope: all 202 required functions from 187 translation units independently rerun sequentially by this reviewer. All MATCH: wave3 66/952 bytes, wave4 130/1612 bytes, six revised accepted functions/492 bytes. Total reviewed 3056 bytes; only 196 functions/2564 bytes are new candidate credit. The five FAIL rows concern recovered source interfaces, not byte mismatches or demonstrated regressions in the unchanged original image.

Source review covered every required body: two independent read-only source slices examined all 51 wave3 units/66 functions and 130 wave4 units/functions; parent directly reviewed six revised accepted units, all twelve shared headers, both new CPP bodies and the high-risk interface/dispatch paths. Source-slice findings were independently re-derived by the record author from fresh original packets before inclusion. Slice agents made no edits, builds, tests or submissions.

Model armlink5-inline-branchnop-v2 is explicitly selected in every independent match. Observed 89 rewrite-bearing functions and 90 operations exactly equal prepare and both full-build receipts: 86 branchnop plus four inline_nop. Every branchnop destination is the next instruction. Every credited function is independently confirmed as an ordinary ARM catalogue owner of the exact extent; no multi-entry owner, veneer, SVC body or compiler-helper classification is credited.

Read docs/REVIEWING.md step 6 and docs/LINKER.md. Four inlined-call choices in func_00185cc0, func_00185d1c and func_0017e7c4 are explicitly marked INFERENCE in source. Fresh original packets establish argument preparation and NOP positions, not the erased target identities. Selected targets are eligible original four-byte ARM return-only functions with no pool/interior entry. The original call graph and whether tailreorder or source order placed wrappers are not recovered. No credited rewrite depends on conditional single-instruction I3 behavior.

Branch-to-next equality does not establish an original C prototype. This qualification does not waive positive receiver evidence: F01-F05 are concrete pointer/const/float/callback contradictions that byte-equivalent wrappers concealed. Other unknown wrapper signatures remain qualified as documented. Return-only void(void) entries are supported as empty implementations, but their historical parameters/return types are not determined by bytes or pointer evidence alone; they are not proven unused.

Integration evidence checked independently: func_00101784 and func_00109a48 test func_00122500 result against zero; func_00109a48 overwrites r0 at 0x10a694 after func_00122510 without using its result. The latter void return remains inference for unknown indirect consumers. Accepted cleanup func_0011f080 uses the pointer returned through func_0013714c/00137150. Destructor chains also support func_0018f7f0 pointer preservation.

Array destruction was traced into the actual func_00100c80 -> func_0019f6b4 reverse loop. It supplies each element pointer and independently returns the allocation cookie base; it discards callback r0. Thus void* return on func_001ef880/001ef884 is a consistent chosen source contract, not a return requirement proven by callback result use.

Manual CPP checks remain under the recorded waiver, not full mechanical type/const checking. FramebufferBinding output-pointer offsets and the shared func_00130e24 interface agree with original func_001245b0. DrawingSystem widths, unsigned RGB conversions, pointer-return vtable call and shared render functions agree with original func_0019f170. The actual func_0011d330 consumer routes 0x4500 color/depth bits and reads clear-color fields at 0x660-0x66c. Concrete installed target classes and whole-program heap/type aliases remain partial.

Partial-prefix qualification: func_001470c8 forwards the correct manager lock address +0x1c4. Local ManagerLock represents only the first word; original 0x195ec4 additionally writes lock+4/+8. No allocation, sizeof, array stride, copy or other extent-dependent use of that partial definition was found; original manager construction accesses a larger object. This is not promoted to a corruption or undersized-allocation finding.

Existing archive selectors func_0014a2f0/00183c54 preserve missing-block null dereferences with ORIGINAL BUG annotations.
